mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 8.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a weakening housing market, which is a key component of consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100) and rising unemployment (UNRATE above 7.5%), the economy is in an early contraction phase, reducing corporate earnings growth and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100 and UNRATE > 7.5%, or the Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained year-over-year CPI inflation increase above 3.0% signals rising inflation expectations, prompting Federal Reserve tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls above 100,000 monthly additions supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 100,000, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion phase (RSAFS above 400,000 million dollars and HOUST above 650,000 units), overheating risks prompt Federal Reserve tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 400000 and HOUST > 650, or the Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a robust housing-led consumption boom, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST grow, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
